ideas.reasoning: B best preserves an executed-feedback interpretation: switching distances describe decisions the saturated controller actually makes, whereas A describes network gain that saturation can erase. The near-zero clamped differences reflect genuine local constancy, not a guaranteed null success contrast; widening the neighborhood changes the question to regional switching structure, and neither representation resolves the strongly off-distribution query states. A query-only feasibility audit offers the most information per episode and LLM call; R-049 should receive the next rollout budget while this representation issue is resolved.

question: R-048 started (git b222600) and I stopped it after block 0's parent (80 gait episodes, seed 4210) and the expert queries (672 queries, no episode), before any arm episode; one LLM call for raw_labels slot 0 was in flight when killed and never reached the ledger. Reason: the PPO expert is bang-bang. On its own 12 demonstration episodes 99.98% of executed action components are at exactly +/-1 (every one of the 20 joints), and at the gait's states 99.7% of its raw (pre-clamp) outputs are beyond +/-1. I implemented the sensitivities as half the difference of CLAMPED actions under +/-h perturbations (h = 10% of each coordinate's 5-95 percentile range over the demonstration: offset_x 0.00096 m, offset_y 0.00073 m, offset_z 0.0032 m, axial_rate 0.86 rad/s, finger flexion 0.023-0.045 normalised units). With clamping, almost every sensitivity is exactly 0 except where an action switches sign inside +/-h, so the treatment packet would be mostly zeros and the contrast would be null by construction of my representation, not by the hypothesis. Also: the gait's states sit far from the expert's (median distance 82 step-units, max 129, in h-scaled coordinates), so the queries are strongly off-distribution. Options I see: (A) report sensitivities of the RAW pre-clamp outputs (the network's local gain before saturation), labelled as such, plus the executed sign; (B) keep clamped outputs but replace finite-difference magnitudes with the switching structure: for each coordinate and action, whether and at what signed displacement within a wider range (e.g. +/-1 demo range) the executed action flips sign; (C) both; (D) stop R-048 as uninformative for a bang-bang expert and record it. Which representation preserves the hypothesis (the expert's local feedback map is more useful than isolated labels), and how should block 0 be handled: reuse its parent record (gait-only, independent of the representation) and recompute evidence from the saved raw outputs (A) or with one more query process (B), restarting both arms in every block with the amended packet? The raw-label arm's padding target changes with the sensitivity packet length, so both arms' requests change.
